title: commentlint config
description: Schema for .commentlintrc.json / .commentlintrc.jsonc, the config file commentlint discovers by searching upward from the working directory. Comments (// and /* */) are stripped before parsing, so a schema-validating editor should treat this file as JSONC.

$schema.description: URL of this schema, for editor autocomplete. Ignored by commentlint itself.

threshold.description: Gate cut: a comment scoring at or above this is reported. Omit to use the model's own calibrated cut, which is what most projects should run.

limit.description: Most findings to print; the rest are still counted. Omit for no limit.

minLength.description: Skip comments shorter than this many characters.

exclude.description: Extra gitignore-style patterns to skip, on top of .gitignore and .commentlintignore.

ignorePath.description: Extra ignore files to read, beyond .gitignore and .commentlintignore.

withNodeModules.description: Scan node_modules too. Off by default.

cache.description: Cache findings between runs, keyed on file stamp and the model's bytes.

cacheStrategy.description: "metadata" trusts mtime and size; "content" hashes file contents instead, which is slower but survives a checkout that skips mtimes.

backend.description: Which backend scores comments: "linear" (what ships) or "encoder".

model.description: Model directory to load, resolved relative to this file. A "//"-prefixed path resolves from the git repository root instead.

npm.description: Settings read by the npm wrapper, not by commentlint itself.

fetch.description: Fetch a specific commentlint ref (tag or commit SHA) as a runnable source tree instead of using the bundled/system Python install.

ref.description: Git ref (tag or commit SHA) to fetch and run.

preferSystem.description: Prefer a system-installed commentlint over the npm-managed Python venv.

markdown.description: Scan .md/.markdown files during directory walks. The shipped model was trained on code comments, so a markdown finding is reported as experimental.

markdownFiles.description: Always check these markdown files, regardless of "markdown". They ride along with a walk -- the default scan root or an explicit directory -- added on top of it rather than in place of it. Once this is non-empty, "markdown" no longer opts every .md/.markdown file in the tree into the walk -- only the files named here are checked. Naming specific files on the command line, with no directory among them, restricts the scan to exactly those files instead; this list does not ride along with that.

splitSentences.description: Score each sentence of a prose comment or markdown chunk on its own, instead of scoring the whole comment as one unit. A comment that mixes one bad sentence into several good ones is otherwise judged by its average, which can wash the bad sentence out.

disableRules.description: Rule ids never to report. The gate that decides whether a comment is flagged at all still runs over every rule; disabling one only changes which rule a finding is named after.

enableRules.description: Rule ids to turn back on even though they ship off by default (C10, C11, C13, P4, P10 -- style calls the taxonomy can't settle for every codebase).

unicodeWhitelist.description: Codepoints and ranges that rule C13 (no non-Latin-1 characters in a comment) lets through. Each entry is either "U+XXXX" for one codepoint or "U+XXXX-U+YYYY" for an inclusive range. C13 ships off by default, so this only matters once it is turned on with enableRules.

languageExtensions.description: Extra file extensions for the three supported language families, on top of their built-in defaults ("c-style": .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs/.mts/.cts, "python-style": .py/.pyi, "markdown": .md/.markdown). An extension can belong to only one family. "c-style" reuses the TS/JS extractor, which is a fair stand-in for other // and /* */ languages.

extends.description: Inherit from another config file; this file's own keys win over the parent's. A "//"-prefixed path resolves from the git repository root, the same as "model" and "markdownFiles".
